problem:
Which of the following are square matrices?

$$
K=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}],\,M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

examples.problem:
Which of the following are square matrices?

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
examples.worked_solution:
- $U$ is *not* a square matrix since the numbers of rows and columns are not the same. It has $2$ rows and $3$ columns, so it's a $2 \times 3$ matrix.

- $W$ is a square matrix since it has the same number of rows and columns. It has $3$ rows and $3$ columns, so it is a $3 \times 3$ matrix.

- $Z$ is a square matrix since it has the same number of rows and columns. It has $2$ rows and $2$ columns, so it is a $2 \times 2$ matrix.

Therefore, $W$ and $Z$ are square matrices.

feedback.problem:
Which of the following are zero matrices?

$$
H=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,I=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0.1 & 0.1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,G=[\begin{aligned}0\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
- $H$ is a zero matrix since *all* its entries are zeros.

- $I$ is *not* a zero matrix since some of its entries are not zeros (for instance, ${i}_{12}=0.1\ne 0$).

- $G$ is a zero matrix since *all* its entries are zeros.

Therefore, only $H$ and $G$ are zero matrices.
